levelNote: Foundational UGC-NET questions on the Black Death, the Peasants' Revolt, Chaucer, Langland, Gower, the Gawain Poet, and Wycliffe.

questions.question: In which years did the first major outbreak of the Black Death (Great Plague) sweep across England during the Age of Chaucer?
questions.explanation: The fierce epidemic of plague known as the Black Death first broke out in England in 1348-1349, sweeping away more than a third of the population.
questions.src: user-supplied: Upkar Guide Book & Course Hero Canterbury Tales

questions.question: In which year did the Peasants' Revolt (also known as Wat Tyler's Rebellion) take place in England?
questions.explanation: The Peasants' Revolt (Wat Tyler's Rebellion) took place in 1381 and accelerated the decline of serfdom.
questions.src: user-supplied: Easy Handbook For NET English Literature & Upkar Guide Book

questions.question: Which fourteenth-century religious reformer is famously known as 'The Morning Star of the Reformation'?
questions.explanation: John Wycliffe (1324-1384) is called 'The Morning Star of the Reformation' for challenging papal authority and translating the Bible into English.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: What name was given to the followers and 'poor priests' sent out by John Wycliffe to spread his reformist teachings across England?
questions.explanation: John Wycliffe sent disciples known as Lollards or 'poor priests' throughout England to preach gospel truth directly from the Bible.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: From which language did John Wycliffe and his associates translate the Bible into Middle English in the 1380s?
questions.explanation: Wycliffe's Bible (c. 1380-1382) was translated directly from the Latin Vulgate into Middle English.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which title was earned by John Wycliffe for his landmark 1382 translation of the Bible into the English vernacular?
questions.explanation: Wycliffe's translation of the Bible in 1382 earned him the title 'Father of English Prose'.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which Pope issued five papal bulls against John Wycliffe in 1377, accusing him on 18 counts of heresy and calling him 'the master of errors'?
questions.explanation: Pope Gregory XI issued five bulls (church edicts) against Wycliffe in 1377, accusing him on 18 counts of heresy and calling him 'the master of errors'.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which war between England and France began in 1337-1338 during the reign of King Edward III and shaped the political backdrop of Chaucer's age?
questions.explanation: The Hundred Years' War between England and France began in 1337-1338 during the reign of Edward III.
questions.src: user-supplied: Easy Handbook For NET English Literature

questions.question: At which university did John Wycliffe serve as a scholastic philosopher, theologian, and seminary professor?
questions.explanation: John Wycliffe was an English scholastic philosopher, theologian, biblical translator, reformer, and seminary professor at the University of Oxford.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Geoffrey Chaucer lived through the reigns of which three successive English monarchs?
options: Edward II, Edward III, and Richard II
Edward III, Richard II, and Henry IV
Richard II, Henry IV, and Henry V
Henry III, Edward I, and Edward II
questions.explanation: Chaucer was born during the reign of Edward III (1327-1377), lived through Richard II (1377-1399), and died during the reign of Henry IV (1399-1413).
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which English royal duke served as Geoffrey Chaucer's chief patron and later married Philippa Roet's sister, Katherine Swynford?
options: Thomas of Woodstock, Duke of Gloucester
Edmund of Langley, Duke of York
John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster
questions.explanation: John of Gaunt (fourth son of Edward III and Duke of Lancaster) was Chaucer's patron and later married Katherine Swynford, sister of Chaucer's wife Philippa Roet.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Chaucer's elegiac dream-vision 'The Book of the Duchess' (1369) was written to commemorate the death of which noblewoman?
options: Elizabeth de Burgh, Countess of Ulster
questions.explanation: Chaucer's The Book of the Duchess (1369) is an allegory on the death of Blanche of Lancaster, wife of his patron John of Gaunt.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which Italian work by Giovanni Boccaccio served as the primary source for the plot of Chaucer's 'Troilus and Criseyde'?
questions.explanation: The plot of Chaucer's 8,239-line poem Troilus and Criseyde was taken largely from Boccaccio's Il Filostrato.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In which work did Geoffrey Chaucer introduce the heroic couplet (decasyllabic rhyming couplet) into English verse for the first time?
questions.explanation: Chaucer used the heroic couplet for the first time in English literature in The Legend of Good Women (1385).
questions.src: user-supplied: Easy Handbook For NET English Literature

questions.question: What is the rhyme scheme and line count of the 'Rhyme Royal' (Chaucerian stanza) used by Chaucer in 'Troilus and Criseyde' and 'The Parliament of Foules'?
questions.explanation: Rhyme Royal (or Chaucerian stanza) consists of seven ten-syllable lines rhyming ABABBCC.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which dream-vision poem by Chaucer is thought to commemorate the 1382 marriage of King Richard II to Anne of Bohemia through a conference of birds on St. Valentine's Day?
questions.explanation: The Parliament of Foules (1382) is a 699-line poem in rhyme royal describing a conference of birds choosing mates on St. Valentine's Day, commemorating Richard II's marriage to Anne of Bohemia.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which unfinished dream-poem by Chaucer shows a close resemblance to Dante's 'Divine Comedy' and features an eagle as the poet's guide?
questions.explanation: Chaucer's The House of Fame (1380) closely resembles Dante's Divine Comedy and features an eagle who guides the poet to the Palace of Fame.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: At which inn in Southwark do the pilgrims assemble before setting out for the shrine of St. Thomas Becket in 'The Canterbury Tales'?
questions.explanation: The pilgrims gather at the Tabard Inn in Southwark, owned by the jovial Host, Harry Bailly.
questions.src: user-supplied: Complete Guide for UGC NET

questions.question: What is the name of the jovial Host of the Tabard Inn who proposes the storytelling contest in 'The Canterbury Tales'?
questions.explanation: Harry Bailly (or Bailey) is the Host of the Tabard Inn who proposes the storytelling game and serves as its judge.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: With which two tales does Chaucer's 'The Canterbury Tales' respectively begin and end?
options: Begins with The Miller's Tale and ends with The Pardoner's Tale
Begins with The Clerk's Tale and ends with The Tale of Melibee
Begins with The Squire's Tale and ends with The Manciple's Tale
Begins with The Knight's Tale and ends with The Parson's Tale
questions.explanation: Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales begins with The Knight's Tale and concludes with The Parson's Tale.
questions.src: user-supplied: Easy Handbook For NET English Literature

questions.question: Although 120 stories were originally planned in 'The Canterbury Tales' (two each way per pilgrim), how many tales were actually included in the work?
questions.explanation: Although 120 tales were planned, only 24 tales were included before Chaucer's death.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: What Latin inscription is engraved on the gold brooch worn by the Prioress (Madame Eglentyne) in the General Prologue to 'The Canterbury Tales'?
questions.explanation: Madame Eglentyne (the Prioress) wears a brooch engraved with 'Amor Vincit Omnia' ('Love conquers all').
questions.src: user-supplied: Easy Handbook For NET English Literature

questions.question: Which poet in 'The Faerie Queene' praised Geoffrey Chaucer as the 'well of English undefiled'?
questions.explanation: Edmund Spenser in The Faerie Queene praised Chaucer as 'well of English undefiled'.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which critic famously remarked 'Here is God's plenty' regarding the variety of characters in Chaucer's 'The Canterbury Tales'?
questions.explanation: John Dryden praised Chaucer's characterization with the famous phrase 'Here is God's plenty' and called him 'The father of English poetry'.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: On which hills does the dreamer Will fall asleep at the opening of William Langland's allegorical poem 'Piers Plowman'?
questions.explanation: The narrator Will lies down on the Malvern Hills in Worcestershire on a May morning and falls asleep to experience the dream visions of Piers Plowman.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Into which two principal parts is William Langland's 'The Vision of Piers the Plowman' divided?
questions.explanation: Piers Plowman is divided into two distinct parts: Visio (the vision of Piers) and Vita (the lives of Dowel, Dobet, and Dobest).
questions.src: user-supplied: Easy Handbook For NET English Literature

questions.question: What is the subject of the very first vision seen by the dreamer in William Langland's 'Piers Plowman'?
options: The Seven Deadly Sins at Confession
questions.explanation: The first vision in Piers Plowman is that of a 'Field Full of Folk' situated between the Tower of Truth and the Dungeon of Wrong.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In the 'Vita' section of Langland's 'Piers Plowman', which three allegorical figures does the dreamer seek in his spiritual quest?
questions.explanation: The second part (Vita) of Piers Plowman is a series of visions titled 'The Search for Dowel, Dobet, and Dobest' (do well, do better, do best).
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: What term is used for the individual sections or cantos into which William Langland's 'Piers Plowman' is divided?
questions.explanation: Piers Plowman is divided into sections called 'Passus' (Latin for 'step').
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In which Middle English dialect was William Langland's 'The Vision of Piers the Plowman' composed?
questions.explanation: William Langland wrote The Vision of Piers the Plowman in the West Midland English dialect as part of the Alliterative Revival.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In the climax of 'Piers Plowman', with which figure is Piers the Plowman ultimately identified as he triumphs over death?
questions.explanation: The poem rises to its highest intensity in Piers's triumph over death, where Piers finally appears as Jesus Christ before the dreamer wakes to the sound of Easter bells.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In which language did John Gower compose his first major poem, 'Speculum Meditantis' (also titled 'Mirour de l'Omme')?
questions.explanation: Gower's Speculum Meditantis (Mirour de l'Omme) was written in French (Anglo-Norman).
questions.src: user-supplied: Easy Handbook For NET English Literature

questions.question: Which of John Gower's major poems was written in Latin elegiac couplets and gives a vivid dream-vision account of the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 in its first book?
questions.explanation: Vox Clamantis ('The voice of one crying out') is a Latin poem in seven books whose first book is a dream vision recounting the Peasants' Rebellion of 1381.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Which 33,000-line poem by John Gower was written in Middle English and translates as 'The Lover's Confession'?
questions.explanation: Confessio Amantis ('The Lover's Confession') is Gower's 33,000-line Middle English poem structured around the confession of an ageing lover.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In the prologue to the first recension of 'Confessio Amantis', which king did John Gower meet on a royal barge on the River Thames, prompting the commission of the poem?
questions.explanation: In the first recension of Confessio Amantis (1390), Gower describes meeting King Richard II on a barge on the River Thames, where the king asked him to write 'som newe thing'.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In dedicating 'Troilus and Criseyde' to John Gower, what famous epithet did Geoffrey Chaucer bestow upon his contemporary?
questions.explanation: Chaucer dedicated Troilus and Criseyde to John Gower and addressed him with the enduring epithet 'O Moral Gower'.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: In the frame story of John Gower's 'Confessio Amantis', to whom does the ageing lover make his confession?
questions.explanation: Confessio Amantis uses the confession made by an ageing lover (Amans) to the chaplain of Venus (Genius) as its frame story.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: When John Gower revised 'Confessio Amantis' between 1390 and 1392, to which nobleman (later King Henry IV) did he add a new dedication?
questions.explanation: Between 1390 and 1392 Gower revised the conclusion of Confessio Amantis and added a dedication to Henry of Lancaster (Henry Bolingbroke), who replaced Richard II in 1399.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question: Besides 'Sir Gawain and the Green Knight', which three other Middle English poems found in the same manuscript are attributed to the Gawain Poet (Pearl Poet)?
options: The Owl and the Nightingale, Havelok, and King Horn
Vox Clamantis, Confessio Amantis, and Speculum Meditantis
questions.explanation: The Gawain Poet (Pearl Poet) is attributed with four poems in the same manuscript: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, Pearl, Patience, and Cleanness (Purity).
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition & Course Hero Sir Gawain

questions.question: What name is given to the signature five-line rhyming conclusion (a short two-syllable line followed by four rhyming lines ABAB) at the end of each alliterative stanza in 'Sir Gawain and the Green Knight'?
questions.explanation: Each Gawain stanza ends with a short connecting line ('bob') followed by four rhyming lines ('wheel'), collectively called the 'bob and wheel'.
questions.src: user-supplied: Course Hero Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.question: During which holiday celebration does the Green Knight ride into King Arthur's court at Camelot to propose his beheading game?
questions.explanation: King Arthur's court is celebrating New Year's Eve during the Christmas festivities when the Green Knight bursts in to propose the beheading game.
questions.src: user-supplied: LitCharts Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.question: Who is revealed at the end of 'Sir Gawain and the Green Knight' to be the true identity of the Green Knight in his unenchanted human form?
questions.explanation: The Green Knight reveals at the Green Chapel that he is actually Lord Bertilak de Hautdesert, who hosted Gawain at his castle.
questions.src: user-supplied: Course Hero Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.question: Which enchantress is revealed to be the old lady at Castle Hautdesert who orchestrated the Green Knight's challenge to test the pride of Arthur's court and frighten Guinevere?
questions.explanation: The old woman at Bertilak's castle is the sorceress Morgan le Fay (Arthur's half-sister), who enchanted Bertilak to test Camelot.
questions.src: user-supplied: LitCharts Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.question: What symbolic geometric emblem is painted in gold on the outside of Sir Gawain's red shield to represent his five sets of five chivalric and Christian virtues?
options: The Red Cross of St. George
questions.explanation: Gawain's shield is decorated on the outside with a symbolic five-pointed Christian pentangle representing his five virtues.
questions.src: user-supplied: LitCharts Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.question: What is the central genre and subject of the Middle English poem 'Pearl' by the Pearl Poet?
options: An allegorical dream-vision elegy mourning the death of a young child
A chivalric romance about the quest for the Holy Grail
A prose treatise on the translation of the Latin Bible
A political satire on the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
questions.explanation: Pearl is a religious dream-vision elegy mourning the loss of a dead child (likened to a lost pearl).
questions.src: user-supplied: Course Hero Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the socio-economic consequences of the Black Death (1348-1349) in England:
I. It swept away between one-third and two-thirds of the population, creating a severe shortage of agricultural labour.
II. The plague recurred in England in 1362, 1367, and 1370, followed by famine and social unrest.
III. It strengthened the feudal manor system permanently and eliminated the emerging urban middle class.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Black Death killed over a third of England's population in 1348-49, recurred in 1362, 1367, and 1370, and created a labour shortage that weakened feudalism and helped skilled workers demand higher wages (making Statement III false).
questions.src: user-supplied: Upkar Guide Book & Course Hero Canterbury Tales

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the pilgrims in the General Prologue to 'The Canterbury Tales':
I. The Knight, the Parson, the Clerk of Oxford, and the Plowman are idealized portraits whom Chaucer does not satirize.
II. The Plowman is presented as the honest brother of the Parson who helps the poor for the love of Christ.
III. The Canon's Yeoman is one of the original 29 pilgrims described at the Tabard Inn before the journey begins.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Knight, Parson, Clerk, and Plowman (the Parson's brother) are idealized and not satirized. Statement III is false because the Canon and the Canon's Yeoman join the pilgrims later on the road to Canterbury.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question:
Arrange the following three literary periods of Geoffrey Chaucer's career and their representative works in correct chronological order:
1. The English Period (The Canterbury Tales)
2. The French Period (The Romaunt of the Rose and The Book of the Duchess)
3. The Italian Period (The House of Fame, The Parliament of Foules, and Troilus and Criseyde)
Choose the correct sequence:
questions.explanation: Chaucer's career is divided chronologically into the French Period (1359-1372), the Italian Period (1372-1385), and the English Period (1386-1400).
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition

questions.question:
Arrange the animals hunted by Lord Bertilak across the three days of the Exchange of Winnings game in 'Sir Gawain and the Green Knight' in correct chronological order:
1. A cunning fox
2. A herd of deer
3. A fierce wild boar
Choose the correct sequence:
questions.explanation: Bertilak hunts deer on the first day (exchanged for one kiss), a wild boar on the second day (exchanged for two kisses), and a fox on the third day (exchanged for three kisses, while Gawain conceals the green girdle).
questions.src: user-supplied: LitCharts Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.question:
Match List I (Work by John Gower) with List II (Language and Verse Form):
List I:
a. Speculum Meditantis (Mirour de l'Omme)
b. Vox Clamantis
c. Confessio Amantis
List II:
1. Middle English poem of 33,000 lines in octosyllabic couplets
2. Anglo-Norman French poem of 29,945 lines in iambic octosyllables
3. Latin poem of 10,265 lines in elegiac couplets
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Gower's Speculum Meditantis (Mirour de l'Omme) is a 29,945-line French poem; Vox Clamantis is a 10,265-line Latin poem in elegiac couplets; and Confessio Amantis is a 33,000-line Middle English poem.
questions.src: user-supplied: World Literature in Your Fist 3rd Edition
